newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up on technicals, warm weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up on technicals, warm weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher Thursday in an active session, as some heat in Texas and forecasts for warmer weather next week stirred some technical buying and short covering.
July jumped five cents to close at $2.221 per million British thermal units. August settled 5.6 cents higher at $2.233. Most other deferreds ended up by 0.1 to 5.4 cents.

"Cash was up on the weather and we may explore the upside a little more because of the heat, but it better be sustained or things could get pretty bad," said one Midwest trader, adding there was good selling in July ahead of $2.25.
Traders said the recent heat wave in Texas and the Southwest coupled with forecasts next week for warmer Midwest and East Coast temperatures helped trigger today's run.
But most agreed sellers will quickly return if the hot weather fails to stick around.

Chart traders said July's break this morning of resistance at $2.21 turned the technical picture more positive. But they said the spot month needed to close above $2.25 to set up a test of the $2.36-2.37 area. Support was now seen at $2.13, then at $2.055 and $2.

In the cash Wednesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed slightly to about $2.20. Midcon pipes were up a couple of cents to the $2.07 area. New York city gate gas was quoted about two cents higher in the mid-to-high $2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 3.4 cents to $2.276. NYMEX said 51,139 contracts traded, up sharply from Wednesday's revised tally of 22,212.

On the KCBT, July finished up seven cents at $2.09, while deferreds ended five to seven cents higher. The East/West spread narrrowed by two cents to 13.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 177 lots traded, up from Wednesday's total of 155.
